title: Excel Keeps Removing Leading Zeros? Fix CSV Imports Properly
description:
Excel can remove leading zeros and change long numeric-looking identifiers when CSV data is interpreted as numbers. This tutorial shows a safer workflow using Data → From Text/CSV → Transform Data → set identifier columns to Text → Close & Load. It also covers Automatic Data Conversions in current Microsoft 365 / Excel 2024, why 15+ digit identifiers are risky, and why custom formatting is not the same as preserving the underlying CSV value.

Sources: Microsoft Support documentation on leading zeros, large numbers, and data import options.

#excel #csv #powerquery #datacleaning

scenes.title: The problem
scenes.narration: Excel can change numeric-looking identifiers when CSV data is opened and interpreted as numbers.

scenes.title: Identifier versus quantity
scenes.narration: An identifier can contain only digits while still requiring text semantics because its digits represent identity, not magnitude.

scenes.title: Safer CSV import
scenes.narration: Open Excel first, use Data then From Text or CSV, choose Transform Data, set identifier columns to Text, then Close and Load.

scenes.title: Long identifiers and precision
scenes.narration: Numeric values longer than fifteen digits can lose precision, so damaged long identifiers should be re-imported from the original source as text.

scenes.title: Automatic Data Conversions
scenes.narration: Current Microsoft 365 and Excel 2024 versions may provide Automatic Data Conversions settings that can disable leading-zero removal.

scenes.title: Common traps
scenes.narration: Custom number formats change display, and TEXT formulas can rebuild known fixed-width codes only when the original digits still exist.

scenes.title: Verify before export
scenes.narration: Inspect the exported CSV in a plain text editor to confirm leading zeros are physically present in the file before uploading it elsewhere.
